Subject: Conditional erase runbook + carve-outs for cross-border backups

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the call this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy and infra teams:

1) Can you confirm how Redwood treats backup snapshots that contain EU subject data when a customer requests erasure under their DSR? Specifically, is there a staged purge (i.e., primary data erased immediately, backups purged within an N-day window), and how do you handle evidence retention for ongoing investigations?

2) We have a few subprocessors in APAC and an S3 provider that may replicate metadata across regions. Please attach the current subprocessor snapshot and highlight which subprocessors hold immutable backups vs. transient snapshots.

3) For forensics: if we require a temporal carve-out (retain logs for X days beyond delete to support an active investigation), can Redwood scope that to an account-level exception and provide audit-proof evidence (time-stamped exports + chain-of-custody notes)?

We need this information to close the DPA amendment and sign-off from our CISO by next Thursday.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Julie

--
Julie Morris
Sr. Privacy Counsel | Acme Health
julie.morris@acmehealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Conditional erase runbook + carve-outs for cross-border backups

Julie —

Thanks for the clear list. Summary answers up front, followed by an attached runbook and matrix: retention_matrix_karthik_v2.xlsx + forensic-carveout-runbook-2026-08.pdf.

1) Backup purge cadence: our standard DSR flow erases primary user artifacts immediately (T0). Backups follow a staged purge: snapshots are marked for deletion and removed in the next scheduled snapshot purge window (default 30 days). For EU accounts with cross-border replication, we can offer a shortened purge SLA of 7 days when requested in a DPA clause.

2) Subprocessors: sending the current snapshot (see CSV attachment). The CSV flags whether a subprocessor holds immutable backups (retention beyond purge window) vs. transient snapshots. Most cloud-object stores we use are transient by default; a small set of archival partners hold immutable restores for compliance (we highlight them in the CSV).

3) Forensics carve-outs: we can support account-level temporal carve-outs. The process is:
  - Customer requests carve-out via support + signed Acknowledgement (DocuSign link included).
  - Redwood marks affected objects with a forensics tag (immutable flag) and moves copies to a sealed evidence bucket.
  - We provide a time-stamped manifest and HMAC-signed export for chain-of-custody.
  - Carve-outs are duration-limited and require justification (investigation ticket) and explicit sign-off from Redwood Security for >90 days retention.

Next steps I propose: legal to confirm wording for the 7-day purge SLA option in the DPA, ops to validate runbook steps with their team, and a signed DocuSign ack to enable any account-level carve-outs.

Attaching runbook and matrix — please review and flag anything that needs expansion.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Adding legal perspective —

Karthik's summary is fine but we need tighter language in the DPA amendment for two items:

• Scope and timing: define "shortened purge SLA" precisely (e.g., "Snapshots containing Customer Data will be purged within 7 calendar days from the purge-marking event").
• Subprocessor obligations: require subprocessors that hold immutable backups to provide the same purge commitment or to allow Redwood to control the purge (contractually).

Also: carve-outs for forensics are acceptable as an exception path, but we must require a written justification and an escrowed audit trail (we can reference our standard evidence manifest template in the runbook). If Acme wants >90 days, that should be an enterprise addendum with SLA/cost implications.

Kimberly

Technical notes from infra/ops:

• Snapshot lifecycle: we tag snapshots at T0 and schedule purge jobs that run in a window every 24 hours. For the 7-day SLA we need to ensure replication lag windows are accounted for — recommend a 48-hour safety buffer to catch cross-region rambles (so operationally target 5 days + 48h replication reconciliation).
• Evidence manifest: we can produce HMAC-signed manifests with object checksums, timestamped by our KMS. We store manifests for 12 months by default.
• Immutable backup partners: two partners (ArchiveStor, LongKeep) keep WORM-style archives. They will require separate contractual terms; we will include a subprocessor callout and the CSV indicates which accounts are impacted.

Action items for ops: I will run a scoped test against an EU account next week to validate the 7-day flow and replication reconciliation and share logs/output.

-Rishi
